title: IRC: a keyed call starting elsewhere should be a notice, not a silence or a trap
description:
Raised 2026-11-23 when Mark asked what an IRC user does about a call.

THE SITUATION. IRC already carries the LINK kind of call
(bead mimid-1wgh.114.3: the `call` command, Store::send_call, the ACTION
line). It cannot carry the KEYED kind: a stock IRC client has no media
stack, so there is nothing to hand a media secret to, and no way to
exchange SDP.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT:

1. A KEYED CALL STARTED ELSEWHERE must be visible. The announcement of
   bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 arrives as a message in the parent chat, so IRC
   will render whatever text it carries -- that is the point of putting
   the human-readable sentence in a message rather than only in an
   extension key. What IRC should NOT do is show it as a joinable
   thing. A notice naming who started it, and saying this client cannot
   join, is the honest rendering.

2. IRC MUST NOT OFFER TO START ONE. A `/call` that hosted a
   parent-dependent room from IRC would make a room nobody on IRC could
   join with media: the user would see a call that silently does
   nothing. If the command is offered at all it should refuse with a
   sentence saying why, which is more use than a call that fails
   quietly.

DO NOT confuse this with giving IRC the keyed call. It cannot have it.
This bead is about the two ways IRC can be wrong about a call it cannot
join.
